sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains the correspondence between the three aspects of Israel (Yaakov, Israel, Yeshurun) and the three aspects of Torah: inheritance (through clarifications), study for its own sake (drawing down revelation), and the gift of Torah (pleasure beyond comprehension).

translations.translation: And this is the connection of these three matters in Israel
(Yaakov,
Israel and Yeshurun)
to the three matters in Torah,
that the matter of inheritance in Torah, which is from the side of the clarifications
[that through the clarifications of Torah one inherits the lights of Tohu,
as above in section 2],
is from the aspect of Yaakov,
for the service of clarifications is in the aspect of Yaakov.
And the matter of "prepare yourself to study Torah,"
that through engaging in Torah for its own sake the revelation of Torah as it is above is drawn down
(the innerness of Torah),
is from the aspect of Israel,
for the engagement in Torah of the aspect of Israel is
(not in order to clarify clarifications,
but rather)
in order to draw down a revelation of G‑dliness.
And the matter of the gift of Torah, which is the drawing down of the delight of Torah
(which is beyond comprehension)
that is beyond division, is from the aspect of Yeshurun.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the Torah is called an inheritance, given that the explanation above relates it to the act of inheriting, while the simple meaning is that the Torah itself is an inheritance.

translations.translation: And it must be understood,
that according to the above explanation,
the reason the Torah is called by the name "inheritance" is because the Torah brings about inheritance
(that through the clarifications through Torah one inherits the lights of Tohu),
but the meaning of "Torah... is an inheritance"
(simply,
for a verse does not depart from its simple meaning)
is,
that the Torah itself is an inheritance.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the inheritance of Torah, where the heir stands in the place of the testator, is superior even to the gift of Torah, and this aspect is connected to the name Yaakov as the essential name shared equally by all Israel.

translations.translation: And it can be said,
that the matter of the inheritance of Torah
(according to the interpretation that the Torah itself is an inheritance)
is higher even than the matter of the gift of Torah.
For that which is brought above from the discourses that inheritance is lower than a gift,
is
because inheritance is from the side of the existence of the heir
(who is a relative of the testator)
and is not dependent on the will of the testator,
whereas a gift is from the side of the will of the giver.
This matter is regarding an inheritance that is
(only)
from the side of kinship.
But regarding an inheritance whose matter is
that the heir stands in the place of the testator
(and consequently inherits his possessions),
it cannot be said that it comes from the side of the existence of the heir,
since the heir is not a separate existence from the testator, but rather stands in the place of the testator.
And on the contrary,
this inheritance is above a gift.
For a gift is from the side of the will of the giver,
but in inheritance
(in this manner)
the heir stands in the place of the testator himself
(which is above his will).
And accordingly, it must be said,
that the reason that regarding the matter of the inheritance of Torah
(which is above even the gift of Torah)
it is stated "an inheritance of the congregation of Yaakov,"
is because Israel and Yeshurun are names of elevation,
and therefore they pertain to the matter of revelations,
whereas the matter of inheritance, where the heir stands in the place of the testator himself, is revealed in the name Yaakov,
as it is the essential name,
in which all of Israel are equal.
